newsitem.title: USA: Fitch group to tackle growing CBO and CLO market.
newsitem.headline: Fitch group to tackle growing CBO and CLO market.

text.p: Fitch Investors Service on Monday said it will create a separate Loan Products Group to analyze and rate individual bank loans, pooled loan and bond transactions known as collateralized bond obligations (CBOs) and collateralized loan obligations (CLOs).
The new unit will be headed by Robert J. Grossman, executive vice president.

Increasing liquidity of the secondary loan market, the growing role of loan securitization in bank capital management and increased institutional interest in loans as an investment spurred the action, Fitch said. Last year, CBOs and CLOs totaled $1.5 billion, the agency noted.
Fitch rates $10 billion of structured loan transactions and evaluates $20 billion of individual bank loans.
Rating activity of CLOs and loans should double this year from 1996 levels, Fitch said.

The Loan Products Group draws together analysts from Fitch's Industrial and Asset-Backed groups. Under Grossman's direction, Tracy Pridgen, director, leads the CBO/CLO analyses with Mario Verna, associate director. Kevin Lydon, associate director, covers individual loan ratings, Randy Szuch, director, coordinates business development and Keith Foley, managing director, is the liaison between loan ratings and the Industrial Group.

Corporate loans are the last major asset class to be actively securitized by commercial banks, Fitch said. The largest banks increasingly originate and structure loans, then sell them to other institutions such as insurance companies, loan funds, CLOs and other banks.
In the recent $3.7 billion Kmart recapitalization bank loan facility, nearly one-third of the syndicate members were non-bank lenders, Fitch said.

Furthermore, National Westminster Bank Plc's recent $5 billion loan securitization will most likely be the first of many transactions that enable large banks to maintain long- standing client relationships and profitability while freeing up significant amounts of capital, Fitch said.
